description.text: Decriannus served as the official architect for Roman emperor Hadrian, a role that placed him at the heart of imperial architectural projects during the early 2nd century CE. His most notable assignment involved overseeing the reconstruction of the Egyptian city of Alexandria, a major urban center that had suffered extensive damage.

While the historical record offers limited details about Decriannus’s personal life or broader body of work, his association with Hadrian situates him among the architects who helped define the aesthetic and engineering standards of the Roman Empire’s golden age. The surviving references to his involvement in Alexandria underscore the importance of imperial patronage in restoring and enhancing key cities across the empire.

curiosities.text: Decriannus was the official architect of the Roman emperor Hadrian, who repaired the Egyptian city of Alexandria.
